spec: Find the largest value in the dict d, then return a sorted list of all keys that map to that value (there may be one or several). The dict is assumed non-empty.

Given a list of distinct integers, compute the minimum number of swaps needed, where each swap can exchange any two elements, to rearrange the list into ascending order. Return that minimum count as an integer. An empty list or an already-sorted list requires 0 swaps.
Given a string, reverse the characters within each single-space-separated word while keeping the words in their original order. Words remain separated by single spaces in the output.
visible_tests: assert reverse_each_word('a bb ccc') == 'a bb ccc'

spec: Merge two numeric dicts a and b into one containing every key from both. For a key present in both, keep the smaller of the two values; for a key present in only one, keep its existing value unchanged. Return the merged dict without mutating either input.

Given a string s, split it into a list of maximal runs of consecutive characters that are either all letters or all digits, preserving order. Any character that is neither a letter nor a digit acts only as a separator (it never appears in the output) and always forces a break, even between an adjacent letter run and digit run.

Find the keys in d whose value does not occur anywhere else in d (i.e. that value maps back to only this one key). Return a sorted list of those keys. If every value repeats (or the dict is empty), return an empty list.

Return True if the given string is a valid clock time in strict "HH:MM:SS" format: exactly two digits, a colon, two digits, a colon, two digits, with hours 0-23, minutes 0-59 and seconds 0-59. Otherwise return False.
Compute the product of the decimal digits of an integer n, using the digits of its absolute value. If any digit is 0 the product is 0. A single-digit number's product is that digit.
Count the number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] equals target. Return that count as an integer. A list with fewer than two elements returns 0.

Given two dates d1 and d2, each a (year, month, day) tuple with d2 on or after d1, return the calendar difference as a (years, months, days) tuple: the largest whole number of years, then whole months, then remaining days. To keep the calendar arithmetic unambiguous, the day-of-month of d1 is always 28 or less.

Given a string s and a string delims whose individual characters are treated as delimiters, split s into a list of tokens such that both the non-delimiter segments and each individual delimiter character appear in the result, in the order encountered. No empty non-delimiter segments are ever included, but every delimiter character produces its own single-character token.

Given a valid date (year, month, day), compute what percentage of the year has elapsed as of the end of that day, i.e. (day_of_year / days_in_year) * 100 as a float, accounting for leap years. Round the result to 2 decimal places.

Format a string to fit exactly in a fixed-width column: if the string is longer than the width, cut it down to exactly width characters; if it is shorter, pad it on the right with spaces to reach the width.

Compare an old dict a against a new dict b. Return a dict with three keys: 'added' (a sorted list of keys in b but not a), 'removed' (a sorted list of keys in a but not b), and 'changed' (a dict mapping each key present in both with a different value to a tuple of (old_value, new_value)). Two equal or empty dicts give empty results for all three.
Given a list of time strings in 'HH:MM' 24-hour format, return a new list of the same strings sorted in chronological order from earliest to latest.

Write a function that returns the k smallest values from a list, sorted in ascending order, including duplicates. If k is greater than or equal to the length of the list, return all elements sorted ascending. If k is 0, return an empty list.

Write a function that sorts a list of numbers in descending order (keeping duplicate values as separate entries) and returns the difference between the first and second values in that order (largest minus second largest). Return None if the list has fewer than two elements.

Given a check time, a start time, and an end time, each a string "HH:MM", return True if the check time falls within the half-open interval [start, end), and False otherwise. If end is less than or equal to start, assume the interval crosses midnight into the next day.

Count the number of distinct words in a string of whitespace-separated words, treating words that differ only in letter case as the same word. An empty or whitespace-only string has zero distinct words.

Wrap every string in the given list in double quotes, then join them into a natural-language list with commas and 'and' before the last item, following the standard oxford-comma rule (zero items give an empty string, one quoted item is returned alone, two are joined with 'and', three or more use an oxford comma).

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, find the longest word that is itself a palindrome, comparing case-insensitively. If multiple palindromic words share the maximum length, return the one that appears first. If no word is a palindrome, return an empty string.
visible_tests: assert find_longest_palindrome_word('mom went to the store') == 'mom'

spec: Given a string s, a single character ch, a positive integer n, and a replacement string, replace the nth occurrence (1-indexed) of ch in s with replacement, leaving every other character unchanged, and return the result. If ch occurs fewer than n times, return s unchanged.

Given a list of integers and a positive integer k, return the k values that occur most often, ordered from most frequent to least frequent. If two values occur the same number of times, the smaller value comes first. k is guaranteed to be at most the number of distinct values.
Given two strings s1 and s2, each a valid ISO date "YYYY-MM-DD", return True if the date in s1 is on or before the date in s2, and False otherwise.

Given two strings a and b, compute the character multiset distance between them: for every distinct character that appears in either string, take the absolute difference between the number of times it occurs in a and the number of times it occurs in b, and return the sum of these differences over all such characters. Empty strings are handled normally (treated as having zero of every character).

Given a valid date (year, month, day), compute a simplified week number for the year, where week 1 covers days 1-7 of the year, week 2 covers days 8-14, and so on (no ISO 8601 rules, just integer division on the day of year).
Given a birth date and a current date, each as (year, month, day), with current date on or after birth date, return the person's age in full completed years.

Given a list of distinct integers, compute the minimum number of adjacent-element swaps needed to rearrange the list into ascending order, which equals the number of inversions (pairs of positions i < j where arr[i] > arr[j]). An empty list or an already-sorted list requires 0 swaps.

If a filename ends with the same non-empty extension repeated twice in a row, separated by periods (for example 'file.tar.tar'), remove one of the two duplicate trailing extensions so it appears only once (giving 'file.tar'). If the filename does not end this way, return it unchanged.
Convert an integer n between 1 and 3999 inclusive into its Roman numeral string representation, following standard subtractive notation rules (e.g. 4 becomes IV, 9 becomes IX).

Validate that a string contains no character repeated 3 or more times consecutively. Scan the string left to right; if any run of identical adjacent characters reaches length 3, return False. An empty string, or one with no such run, returns True.

Given a local time as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and the local zone's UTC offset in minutes (which may be negative), return a (utc_hour, utc_minute, day_delta) tuple: the UTC time-of-day and the signed number of days the UTC date shifts by relative to the local date.

Given a list of (name, score, age) tuples and an integer k, return the names of the k top entries as a list. Entries are ordered by score descending; ties are broken by age ascending, and further ties by name ascending. If k exceeds the number of entries, return all names in this order.

Given a list of items, remove duplicate values while keeping only the first occurrence of each, preserving the original relative order of the remaining elements. The input list may contain integers or strings and may be empty.

Validate a checksum string of digits where the last character is a check character for the digits before it. Assign ascending weights 1, 2, 3, ... (by position from the left, starting at 1) to the digits before the check character, sum the weighted values, and take that sum modulo 11: if the result is 10 the check character must be 'X', otherwise the check character must be the decimal digit equal to the result. The body (all but the last character) must be non-empty and contain only digits. Return False otherwise.

Write a function that returns a list of the same length as the input, where each output element is the number of distinct values seen in the input list up to and including that position. An empty input returns an empty output.

Write a function that splits a list into two lists based on index parity, returning a tuple (evens, odds) where evens contains the elements at indices 0, 2, 4, ... and odds contains the elements at indices 1, 3, 5, ..., each preserving order. An empty list returns two empty lists.
Write a function that counts the number of maximal runs of consecutive equal elements in a list (the number of groups produced by run-length encoding). Return 0 for an empty list.

Given a start time and end time, each a string "HH:MM", return the elapsed duration as "H:MM" (hours with no leading zero). If the end time is less than or equal to the start time, assume the interval crosses midnight into the next day.
Pad a string on the right with a fill character until its length is a multiple of the given positive integer. If the length is already a multiple, return the string unchanged.
